title: Next.js routing, taken apart
dek: Next.js 16.4 turns an app/ folder tree into a sorted route table, one server entry per URL, prerendered segment files and per-segment prefetch hints, all before the first request. This teardown follows one route, app/sec0/a/[id]/page.tsx, from file to click through the code at v16.4.0, and prices each precomputation with numbers measured on a 2-vCPU machine. It ends with the practices that moved those numbers, and the beliefs the code contradicts.
byline: 14 October 2026 · Subject: vercel/next.js@v16.4.0 (e273d5b2e869), released 6 October 2026 · Read from the source, the docs at the tag and the release posts; timings measured on this machine
description: A teardown of Next.js 16.4 folder routing: file grammar, build, request path, rendering, caching, client router and prefetch, with measured costs.
og_description: Next.js routing read end to end at v16.4.0 (commit e273d5b2): how the app/ tree becomes a route table, a LoaderTree and prerendered segment files; how next start resolves a request; how segments render, cache and prefetch; and what each precomputation costs, measured on a 2-vCPU machine, with the practices that changed the numbers.
